newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa considering taxes on offshore income.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa considering taxes on offshore income.

text.p: The South African Revenue Service is considering ways in which to tax rental, interest, dividend and annuity income earned offshore once exchange controls are lifted, commissioner Trevor van Heerden said on Monday.
Van Heerden told Reuters that this would protect South Africa's revenue base.
"We would allow credit for any tax paid outside, so it is just to ensure that people do not go and invest all their money outside and our tax take drops here," Van Heerden said.
In his maiden budget last week Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced an easing of foreign exchange controls on individuals and corporates.
Van Heerden had been asked by the parliamentary finance committee how the lifting of exchange controls would affect the tax treatment of so-called "passive" income.
A salary is regarded as active income but rental income, interest, dividends and annuities are seen as passive income that could be moved offshore.
"Those are the ones that we want to bring back and tax here. We already deem interest to be from a source here so it is just extending those rules a bit, " Van Heerden said.
